reasons: Status is correctly 'missing': no insurance covenant appears in the cited General Matters sub-clauses, and the rationale reports a document-wide search for 'insurance' returning nothing; the rule expects such a clause for a vendor performing on-site installation/data conversion and ongoing support.

The redline is actionable and minimal: it appends a single new sub-clause (k) to the miscellaneous section without altering existing text (p0149 is preserved verbatim), matching the rule's redline guidance to insert a short insurance paragraph in the general section.

Inserted language tracks the playbook model language and preferred limits (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where Customer Data is processed, workers' comp as required by law, certificates on request), with party names correctly localized to Garman/Sparkling.

Comment is concise, first-person plural, prefixed correctly, accurately explains the change and the on-premises/data rationale, cites the preferred position and offers the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback without lecturing.
Deterministic checks confirm the operation applies and an insurance obligation is now present; no over-flagging or duplication of another rule's commercial term.
